INTERVIEW EXPERIENCE
UBS
Dushant Harinkhede | T.Y  B.Tech CSE
UBS visited our campus on 24rth January 2023 for the On-Campus Internship
Drive.
Eligibility Criteria: 7+ CPI  & more than 70% in 10th and 12th.
Stipend : 40,000
Branches: Computer Engineering, Information Technology, Electronics and
Telecommunication

Internship Test(24 Jan 2023)
There were 60 MCQ questions and 1 code question in the 80-minute test.
Platform for test : Hackerrank
30 MCQs covering JAVA, SQL, and OOPS, and 30 aptitude questions.
As a result, I was able to answer 45–50 questions in around 60 minutes, and I
felt confident that 90–95 percent of them were accurate. I decided to attempt the
coding question after skipping the remaining questions.
1 coding Problem:
In this, our goal was to maximize the bitwise XOR value of the two strings that we
were given.
After finishing my code and clicking "run code," the allotted time expired. My first
thought was whether or not the points for the coding question would count since I
was unable to submit the code. After the test, I did some research online and
discovered that even if we run the code (i.e., compile it at least once), it will still
calculate the score of that compiled code. Since the code was optimized, I was
certain that it would pass all of the test cases. Since I hadn't tried 10-15 MCQ
questions, I was a little anxious about my shortlisting.
After all of this, the test results were announced on January 27, and I was one of
the eight applicants chosen for the next round. The next round to be conducted
was an offline interview round.
Interview Round (50 Minutes- 31 Jan 2023)

For this round, we had to go to Airoli, Mumbai. 30 minutes before my appointed
interview time, I arrived at the office. My first offline interview in my life, to be
honest, made me a little nervous. But in addition to this, I was also confident
because prior to this, I had participated in 5–6 interviews. As a result, I had good
experience with interviews and had gained a lot of experience from my prior
interviews.
As we reached the destination i.e Airoli office they told us to wait and made us sit
in the waiting room. After some time the interviewers arrived and then the
interview began.
Now Interview story begins 😀:
First I greeted both interviewers then they asked me to show my resume. I gave
a copy of my resume to each of them. Then they asked me to introduce myself.
Since this part was prepared by me, I made a good introduction. Then after the
introduction, they started to ask me questions related to my projects. I had 3
projects namely data-map, Rangawardhan site, and cryptokeeda. All of these
were react-based applications. They asked me to explain my projects then I
explained my projects to them. Since they didn't allow me to open my laptop I
made GUI’s of my website on paper and explained each and every functionality.
My explanation impressed both interviewers, and one of them then asked about
my knowledge of cryptocurrency. Actually, I know very little about
cryptocurrencies. She responded by saying that you completed a project on
cryptocurrency despite having little knowledge of the topic. I handled the situation
by explaining that I created the project in order to learn how to fetch data, which
convinced her of my motivation. I made a small mistake here; if you do a project
on any topic, you should be aware of the topic's importance. It's crucial to
understand why you are doing the project, but you should also be aware of its
significance.
They were, however, really impressed by my ability to explain things clearly and
my capacity to respond to any technical queries on my projects.
They continued by asking some DBMS and SQL queries after projects.
1) What is SQL, and how is it different from MySQL?
2) How do delete, drop, and truncate vary from one another?

3) What is your knowledge of joins? List the various join types and describe the
left join.
4) What SQL Null Implies
5) A SQL query
I had no trouble responding to any of the questions, and I typically did so by
creating charts, diagrams, and written queries before explaining. I believe this is
the best method for explaining things to others because our minds process visual
information more effectively than auditory information, so try to explain things by
putting them in writing. (Of course, it also depends on the interviewer and the
time allocated for the interview.)
After that, they began to ask me  questions such as,
"Why do you want to join UBS?"
What distinguishes an investment bank from a retail bank?
What do you envision in the next five years?
Why did you enroll in VJTI?
She then inquired as to my interests, to which I replied that I enjoyed cricket and
listening to music.
We had a quick conversation about cricket because one of the interviewees was
also a lover of the sport. She asked me if I still followed cricket and what was
going on in the game.
As my father is a retired army personnel, they next inquired about my family, and
we had a talk about it as well.
They then questioned me whether I had any further questions after hearing all of
this. In order to demonstrate your interest in the organization, you should ask the
interviewer a question if they ask it of you.
Following this, the interviewer and I were having a casual talk during which she
asked me questions like 1) How will you spend your stipend?

He made some recommendations, including the following: It is commendable that
you are familiar with all the technical aspects of the project, but you should also
be knowledgeable about the subject matter before beginning.
In the interview, I mentioned that I had given up playing cricket because of all the
preparation for my internship. She also advised me to keep playing  games.
As a result, my interview was finished in about 50 minutes. This time, there was
only one interview round, and I must say that the offline interview process was
much better than the online one because it was more interactive. I had a positive
impression of the interview and was hopeful that I would be offered an internship,
so I was looking forward to the outcome.
Result day:
The eighth of January will always be one of my favorite days. Eight days after the
interview, we received a letter in which 6 out of 8 candidates were given
internship offers. Fortunately, I was one of them.
Internship preparation tips:
DBMS and SQL:
1)If you don't have any knowledge of DBMS then you can start with the
knowledge gate youtube channel or gate smashers. Both are good. Personally, I
preferred knowledge gate.
2) You should have gone through all  the interview questions of interviewbit.
https://www.interviewbit.com/dbms-interview-questions/

3)For sql if you are at a very beginner level you can learn sql through gate
smashers or w3school, both are good resources to start with.
4)Now after some hands-on basic sql you can watch this playlist from techftq
youtube channel. It has a good playlist of 7 videos related to interview questions.
https://youtube.com/playlist?list=PLavw5C92dz9HQQ_COgGb7kf_1H8UWUBxO
5) For practicing SQL queries everyone will suggest practicing on hacker rank or
leetcode but I personally liked this site for SQL practice.
https://platform.stratascratch.com/coding?code_type=1
6)Now for me these two blogs were really helpful for SQL interviews.If you have
less time to prepare, like 1 month or so then you can prepare from these two
websites.(but you should have basic knowledge of SQL)
https://www.edureka.co/blog/interview-questions/sql-query-interview-questions#f
etchaddressname → Mostly Covers all important sql query questions
https://techtfq.com/blog/top-20-sql-interview-questions → top 25 important sql
questions
This much is more than enough for sql and DBMS.
OOPS:
1)Since my first language to code was c++ so I did my OOPS in c++ only.
2)One of the best resources to follow for the oops concept for me was code with
harry's youtube channel. If you have time you should definitely watch the CWH
playlist.
https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLu0W_9lII9agpFUAlPFe_VNSlXW5uE0Y
L
3)Try to make your own notes else if you don’t make you can follow these notes
for revision

https://www.linkedin.com/posts/madhavvarjuntthukral-b41564183_oops-ugcPost-
7024321442649378816-xmY4/?utm_source=share&utm_medium=member_andr
oid
It includes all the important questions which are asked in the interview.
4)Don't just study the concepts, implement them in code as well. You may be
asked to demonstrate these concepts in C++ or Java.
5)While preparing concepts of oops like inheritance, polymorphism, etc you
should have the ability to explain these concepts with real-life examples. It shows
that you can implement your study in the real world.
OS :
1)It was the only subject which was least asked to me in my interviews out of 6
company interviews. It was asked in only one and that's also DE Shaw.
2)So from my personal experience don't give much time on this subject just
watch gate smashers os the playlist and make notes and go through interview bit
interview questions.
DSA:
For Binary Search, Stacks, Sliding Window (MUST), Heap - Aditya Verma.
For DP, Trees, and  Graphs - take U forward.
Tips -
1) Always revise the sorting algorithms, basic data structure questions
because they are frequently asked in interviews such as quick sort, merge
sort, stack using a queue, queue using stack, graph traversals, etc.
2) Make notes for each topic that you cover. These could be on some pattern
that you identified in such questions as finding Kth order statistics in
an array being related to a heap or some syntax that you find tough to
remember such as the declaration of the priority queue in C++.

3) Don't hit a trial by submitting your code; it just wastes time. Rather
do a dry run of example input and expected output. You won't be asking an
interviewer to confirm your code multiple times. so develop the habit of
verifying it twice and submitting it once.
4) Sometimes you may be asked to write the driver code, and data structure
implementation along with the algorithm for the given question - in both
online tests and interviews. Do practice writing driver code for a linked list,
tree, and graph questions.
(all these tips of DSA I took it from Pankaj kushlani(our senior) interview
experience as all these tips are really good to follow )
Some other tips :
1) If you are specially preparing for UBS then my tips are :
a) DSA :
1) study all sorting algorithms thoroughly.
2) Study all implementations like stack, queue, and heap
implementation.
3) Mostly they ask questions about the array and linked list data
structure.
4) Sometimes they ask questions about which algo you have studied
and if you have said any graph algo then they can ask you to
implement that too.
b) SQL :
1) The same tips as mentioned above and are applicable to all companies as
well.
c) Projects :
1) One of the most important and easiest things to prepare as it is assumed
that you have made the project and you know each and every functionality
of the project.
2) I will say please study the project topic also like if you have a web app
related to crypto then do some sort of research about crypto like what is
crypto? What are the top cryptos in the world currently? anything related to
crypto news, all these things.

3) If the interview is offline you may not be able to use a laptop so have the
practice explaining every sort of thing about the project without a live
demonstration you can use pen and paper to make a GUI of a Website/app
and explain things.
4) And the most important one is don't fake your projects like you have cloned
a project from GitHub and you have to know an idea about the project
code or you are not able to understand the working of the project.
d) Research :
1) Do good research about the company, I will say visit the site and navigate
through each and every page and make notes and try to connect these
points with your HR interview answers.
2) Research includes the point of difference between Investment banks and
retail banks.
2)Don't be afraid to ask friends for help with the areas you are not good at. For
example, I asked my best friend for advice on how to speak to interviewers and
how to project confidence, and they all helped me work on my attitude.
I had a positive interview experience thanks to my roommates, who conducted
mock interviews with me.
Finally, I would say thank you to all and all the best for the
internship interviews.
